data.title: India's J.K. Cement buys 27% stake in renewable power firm
data.description:
Indian cement maker J.K. Cement (BSE: 532644) has approved buying 27.03% of Clean Renewable Energy KK 1E Private Limited for INR51.45mn ($552,340) , the company said in a filing to the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India on November 19.

The stake will give the company a share of solar power for its Muddapur plant under a captive power arrangement. The company said the deal would raise the proportion of renewable energy in its power mix. It described the investment as part of its plan to make greater use of renewable sources. J.K. Cement will subscribe to 1,101,949 equity shares with a face value of INR10 each and will pay in cash.

The filing listed no government or regulatory approvals as necessary for the transaction. The company said the purchase was not a related party transaction. Neither its promoter, its promoter group nor its group companies hold any interest in the target, according to the filing. Clean Renewable Energy KK 1E is promoted by Hero Rooftop Energy Private Limited and was incorporated in 2024.

Its registered office is in Aerocity, near New Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport. The firm develops and runs a 125.8 MW hybrid project in the southern state of Karnataka, made up of 26.4 MW of wind capacity and solar capacity of 99.4 MWac, or 149.1 MWp. Power from the project is supplied under an open access mechanism, and the power producer's allocation stands at 11.4 MW.

The target company remains at an early stage. It booked turnover of INR400,000 in the 2025-26 financial year, after reporting no revenue in 2024-25. As of March 31, 2026, it posted a net loss of INR4mn and a negative net worth of INR5.6mn.

data.title: Storms slow Western Australia's wheat, barley and canola harvest, industry body says
data.description:
Western Australia's wheat harvest estimate for the 2026 season was largely unchanged from a month ago, an industry body said on Friday, while forecasts for barley and canola production were trimmed after a series of storms disrupted harvesting.

Western Australia is Australia's largest crop-exporting region and one of the world's biggest shippers of grain and canola.

The Grain Industry Association of Western Australia (GIWA) said in a monthly crop report that the state is expected to reap 10.90 million metric tons of wheat this season, up marginally from the October estimate of 10.89 million tons.

Barley production is now estimated at 6.68 million tons, compared with 6.80 million tons a month ago. Canola production is forecast at 4.12 million tons, down from 4.60 million in the previous month.

Harvesting had been running slightly ahead of recent years before several storm events in October and early November disrupted operations across key grain-growing regions.

The southwest and west coast regions have been particularly affected, with rain this week stretching from the midwest to central and eastern growing areas causing further delays.

Harvesting is continuing across the state's major grain-growing regions and is expected to wrap up around year-end.

data.title: Malaysia's Export Growth Hits 5.5 Year High
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Malaysia's export growth accelerated further in October, hitting a 5.5-year high thanks to strong demand for electrical and electronic products.

Exports rose 61.1% from a year earlier to 239.20 billion ringgit, equivalent to $58.16 billion. It eclipsed the 54.5% increase in September and marks the sharpest pace of growth since April 2021. Imports rose 54.4% to 197.41 billion ringgit, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry said Friday.

That resulted in a trade surplus of 41.79 billion ringgit, larger than September's 34.35 billion ringgit surplus.

The median forecast in a Wall Street Journal poll of six economists was for exports to rise 48.4% and imports to increase 44.4%, resulting in a trade surplus of 30.66 billion ringgit.

Malaysia's electronics exports could face fresh headwinds from tighter U.S. restrictions on advanced chip shipments. Washington on Monday announced new rules aimed at limiting China's access to advanced artificial-intelligence computing power through overseas data centers, including those using Nvidia chips.

The U.S. Commerce Department also added Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil to a list of destinations subject to new export licensing requirements for advanced semiconductors.

Malaysia has benefited from the global AI boom, but the new restrictions could pose further risks to its electronics sector, Capital Economics economist Gareth Leather said in a note.

While Malaysia isn't a major chip producer, it is an important hub for chip packaging and testing. The country also manufactures components and equipment used in semiconductor production and testing. Exports from these industries have surged this year.

However, the boost could fade if demand for AI-related products slows next year and stalls in 2028, Capital Economics said.

Exports of manufactured goods, which accounted for 89% of total shipments in October, rose 68% from a year earlier, the data showed. Exports of electrical and electronic products, which made up about 52.5% of the total, rose 87.2%.

On a month-over-month basis, exports rose 10.9% in October, while imports rose 8.8%.

data.title: Malaysia's October exports rise 61.1% y/y, above forecast
data.description:
Malaysia's exports rose 61.1% from a year earlier in October, higher than expectations, government data showed on Friday.

October's exports were expected to grow 46%, according to nine economists surveyed by Reuters.

Imports in October grew 54.4% from a year earlier, data from the statistics department showed. Analysts were expecting a 42% increase.

Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of 41.8 billion ringgit ($10.17 billion) in October, compared to the poll forecast of 34.4 billion ringgit.

data.title: SLS Stock Suffers Worst Rout Since January After $150M Share Sale — But Fresh Filing Has Retail Bulls Saying Sellas Has More Buyout Leverage
data.description:
Key points:
  • Shareholders who don’t buy more shares would see their ownership stakes shrink by about 5.4% under the base offering.
  • Sellas priced 11.54 million new shares at $13 each. That’s 28% below Wednesday’s close but still 74% above where the stock closed Monday, before the trial results came out.
  • In the Regal trial, patients who received Sellas’ GPS leukemia vaccine lived a median of 24 months, compared with 14.7 months for those who received the best available treatment.

Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) logged their worst session since January on Thursday, but a fresh filing put expected net proceeds from its share sale at $140.6 million, fueling debate among retail traders over whether the biotech could turn down a lowball bid.

SLS stock closed at $14.86 on Thursday, two days after positive leukemia trial results sent the stock soaring 156%.

SLS Expects Net Proceeds To Top September Cash

On Wednesday, Sellas priced 11.54 million new shares at $13 each, a 28% discount to Wednesday’s close but still 74% above Monday’s close, before the trial results.

Sellas expects to net $140.6 million from the $150 million offering after fees and expenses, according to its final prospectus. That’s $5.9 million more than the $134.7 million it held in cash and cash equivalents on Sept.30. Underwriters would earn $9 million in commissions on the base deal, which Sellas expected to close on Friday.

Based on the September share count, the offering would lift shares outstanding from 203.5 million to 215.1 million, reducing the ownership stake of shareholders who buy no new shares by about 5.4%. If underwriters buy all 1.73 million additional shares available to them, Sellas expects net proceeds to reach $161.8 million.

Fresh Cash Gives SLS Room To Prepare For GPS Launch

The share sale would give Sellas more room to fund clinical work and prepare for a potential launch of Galinpepimut-S (GPS), the experimental leukemia vaccine behind Tuesday’s rally. In its quarterly filing, Sellas said it had used $22.4 million in cash for operations in the first nine months of 2026 and still expected its cash on hand to cover at least another year of operations.

The next step for GPS is a meeting with the FDA. In the Phase 3 Regal trial, patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who received GPS lived a median of 24 months, compared with 14.7 months for those who received the best available treatment. The patients were in their second or later remission and could not undergo a stem cell transplant. Sellas aims to file for approval in the first half of 2027.

If GPS wins approval, Sellas retains the right to launch it on its own in the U.S. or work with a partner. The company holds sole rights to the vaccine outside Greater China and said in 2024 that it was working with Stifel to explore commercial partnerships.

How Do Retail Traders Feel About SLS?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around SLS jumped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a week ago amid ‘extremely high’ message volume.

One user called the $13 offering price “disappointing” but said the proceeds strengthened the firm's hand. “It also reduces the risk that management will be forced to accept a lowball buyout offer because of financial pressure,” the user said.

View this Stocktwits post

Other users floated Merck (MRK) and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) as possible buyers. A separate user saw a more immediate choice for Sellas: whether to prepare for a U.S. launch on its own or seek a pharmaceutical partner. “I wouldn't interpret the acquisition exception or the size of the financing as evidence of a pending buyout,” the user said.

View this Stocktwits post

SLS stock has surged 294% year-to-date.

data.title: U.S. Chip Curbs Likely to Have Limited Impact on Tencent's AI Business — Market Talk
data.description: The newly introduced U.S. chip curbs will likely have limited impact on Tencent's artificial-intelligence business, Barclays analysts say in a note. Most of its AI agents don't require the highest-performing AI models, powered by the most advanced AI chips, they note. Users are quite happy with flash models, which carry highly economical price tags, they say. Tencent's ability to drive user adoption of its AI work assistant Workbuddy and monetize it is far more significant than having access to most advanced Nvidia chips, they note. Meanwhile, Tencent is on the verge of launching its AI agent for WeChat to all users in China as the costs of running the AI agent, Xiaowei, to support its 1.4 billion WeChat users have now become manageable. Tencent shares are 1.4% lower at 343.20 Hong Kong dollars. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)

data.title: Why Did NVDA, NIO, ONDS Stocks Tumble To 52-Week Lows Today?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia shares hit a 52-week low of $145.71, extending their losing streak to six sessions.
  • Nio shares hit a six-year low on vehicle delivery concerns ahead of earnings. 
  • Ondas faced pressure from dilution and rising cash burn. 

Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Nio Inc. (NIO) and Ondas Holdings (ONDS) stocks tumbled to fresh 52-week lows on Thursday, as mounting China chip export scrutiny, declining electric vehicle deliveries and aggressive share dilution weighed on investor sentiment.

Nvidia and Nio stocks dropped 3%, while Ondas stock tumbled 4%. The sell-off overshadowed Nvidia's AI demand, Nio's recovery ambitions and Ondas' rapid revenue growth.

Nvidia Faces Fresh Questions Over China Chip Exports

Nvidia stock dropped to an annual low of $145.71, extending its losing run to six trading sessions. The stock has shed approximately 19% since Nov. 8 as congressional scrutiny surrounding its China-related business intensified.

According to a New York Times report, documents released by members of the House Foreign Affairs Committee revealed that the Commerce Department had authorized exports involving more than 800,000 advanced AI processors to Chinese organizations by May 11. Some recipients reportedly appeared on lists identifying companies with military connections.

One disclosure drew particular attention to Nvidia's April application seeking permission to supply more than 40,000 H200 processors to New Century Lettall Data Service. The company has alleged connections to Megaspeed and Alice Huang, figures linked with the controversy surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

Additionally, California Attorney General Rob Bonta has subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation into whether its chips were illegally exported to China. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

Nio Slides As ONVO Deliveries Contract

Nio stock reached its lowest level in six years as investors reacted to disappointing October sales and weakness across Chinese-listed stocks. The automaker delivered 34,246 vehicles last month, representing a 15.2% year-on-year decline. Its family-oriented ONVO division accounted for much of the weakness, with shipments falling 51.7% to 8,383 units. Deliveries under the primary NIO brand, meanwhile, increased 5.7%.

Nio must now average 42,900 deliveries during November and December to reach its fourth-quarter target of exceeding 40,000 vehicles per month. Gross margins will be a major focus in Nio’s Dec.1 Q3 earnings amid aggressive pricing competition in China's EV market. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bullish’.

Ondas Investors Focus On Dilution And Cash Burn

Ondas stock dipped to a yearly low of $4.2, overshadowing strong Q3 revenue and its growing order backlog. Q3 revenue reached $167.5 million, compared with $50.7 million in revenue for the entire 2025 fiscal year. Its backlog also expanded 36% from the previous quarter to $835 million.

However, investors are concerned that Ondas has issued too many new shares, diluting existing shareholders' ownership. The company raised $830 million through an equity offering in 2025 and another $959 million in the first half of 2026. Its spending also increased, with operations using $141 million in Q3.

Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bearish’.

So far this year, NVDA, NIO and ONDS stocks have declined between 21% and 56%.

data.title: Alibaba puts quixotic faith in made-in-China chips
data.description:
By Robyn Mak

Boss Eddie Wu is confident the $208 bln tech group can rely on domestic silicon to offset US export controls and train and deploy AI models. Tencent is optimistic too. Yet Washington's tightening controls and China's few foundries make a protracted chip shortage more likely.

Full view will be published shortly.

Follow Robyn Mak on X.

CONTEXT NEWS

China's Alibaba on November 19 reported revenue of 271.5 billion yuan ($40.7 billion) in the quarter ended September 30, an increase of 10% year-on-year. Revenue from its AI Cloud and Compute Services division rose 53% in the period, to 61 billion yuan.

Chief Executive Eddie Wu said new US restrictions will affect next year's products and services, but the company expects to "ramp up very significantly" production capacity of its in-house T-Head chips by 2027. He added the company might target cloud revenue growth of 30% to 45% in 2027, rebounding to 50% or higher in 2028 and putting Alibaba on track to hit its previously stated 2030 targets of $100 billion in external cloud revenue and a 20% EBITDA margin.

The US Commerce Department on November 16 announced interim licensing requirements on overseas data centre operators and contract chip manufacturers serving Chinese customers.

data.title: China yuan recovers from one-month low on exporter demand, strong dollar caps gain
data.description:
China's yuan on Friday bounced from a more than one-month low against the US dollar that it hit a day earlier, as corporate repatriation offset the impact of a continuing dollar rally.

The Chinese currency had declined in both onshore and offshore markets to its weakest since mid-October before a pick-up in seasonal corporate demand, with companies taking advantage of a strong dollar to convert foreign-currency receipts, traders said.

Exporters typically convert foreign earnings into yuan at the end of the calendar year and ahead of the Lunar New Year due accounting and administrative requirements, as well as demand for cash to fund bonuses and holiday-related expenses. This usually bumps up the yuan in December and January.

The onshore yuan rebounded from 6.6950 a dollar, its weakest since October 14, to trade at 6.6715 as of 0245 GMT. Its offshore counterpart last fetched 6.6746.

Prior to market open, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) set its midpoint rate — around which it allows daily yuan movement of as much as 2% either side — at 6.7131, 400 pips weaker than a Reuters' estimate of 6.6731.

The firmer dollar and market expectations of more aggressive interest rate hikes from the US Federal Reserve to tame inflation have weighed on the value of emerging market currencies, particularly after minutes of the Fed's latest meeting showed policymakers considered additional tightening.

However, analysts expect the yuan to appreciate through 2027.

"We expect a gradual appreciation in the renminbi to continue through 2027," said Jeremy Zook, lead analyst for China at Fitch Ratings.

"Nevertheless, we expect the Chinese authorities to lean against a fast degree of appreciation as they don't want to significantly dampen export performance given weaknesses in domestic demand."

A sizable current account surplus and easing capital outflow pressure should support the yuan, said Yu Song, chief China economist at UBS Securities.

"The PBOC may continue to allow market forces to drive the change and only step in when the pace is considered too rapid," he said, expecting the yuan to finish this year at 6.6 a dollar and strengthen to 6.25 by the end of next year.

Separately, the PBOC held its benchmark lending interest rates on Friday for the 18th successive month, matching market expectations.

data.title: El Salvador's Bukele seeks unprecedented third term as leader
data.description:
Key points:
  • Polls show Bukele has commanding 55% to 70% support
  • Security crackdown popular at home and in region
  • Victory in February vote would grant him third term in office
  • Critics oppose reforms that ended limits on reelection

El Salvador's Nayib Bukele registered his candidacy on Thursday to seek an unprecedented third term as president in February elections that he is expected to win, even as critics have raised concerns that his authority is unchecked.

The ruling Nuevas Ideas party has scrapped term limits, a move the opposition and rights groups say will allow Bukele to consolidate power indefinitely without institutional checks and balances. The government has rejected those accusations.

Bukele, 45, now officially running alongside Vice President Felix Ulloa for a third consecutive term, secured his party's nomination in July. He finalized his registration ahead of the Thursday deadline for candidates.

As he arrived to file his paperwork, a crowd of supporters gathered outside the Supreme Electoral Tribunal, cheering and chanting "six more years." After signing his registration, Bukele thanked the crowd and said the country was moving toward a democratic election that would feature "freedom of expression."

After overseeing an aggressive crackdown on organized crime, Bukele is the clear favorite to win the presidential vote. He has support of 55% to 70%, according to polls that also show his party well ahead of opposition parties polling in single digits.

Bukele will face four opposition candidates, including Maytee Iraheta of the right-wing Nationalist Republican Alliance (ARENA) and Rafael Aguirre of the left-wing Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front (FMLN).

While rights groups say Bukele's policies, including a state of emergency imposed in 2022, have harmed due process and innocent lives, the government has dismissed accusations of authoritarianism and said it is prioritizing victims of violence, not gang members.

El Salvador's security crackdown has also boosted Bukele's popularity in the region, with other governments seeking to replicate its model.

In October, El Salvador sent more than 2,000 troops to fight armed gangs in Haiti, in a rare foreign intervention after four Salvadoran members of a UN-backed force went missing. Some analysts said the move, welcomed by Haiti, sought to export Bukele's model regionally.

INCREASING POWER

A former publicist, Bukele was expelled from the FMLN in 2017 and came to power in 2019, ending three decades of rule by ARENA and FMLN.

Two years later, the Supreme Court ruled that sitting presidents could seek reelection, in a break from the Central American nation's past.

Bukele's subsequent landslide election victory in 2024 also handed his party control of Congress, which in 2025 approved a constitutional amendment allowing presidents to run for reelection an indefinite number of times.

The amendment also extended leaders' terms to six years, abolished second-round votes and rescheduled the presidential election to February 2027 to coincide with the legislative and municipal elections.

The two main opposition parties have questioned the mass arrests in Bukele's security crackdown, denouncing many as arbitrary, and have promised to repeal the state of emergency.

The president's Nuevas Ideas party, which holds 54 of the 60 seats in Congress, has said it will also field candidates in the remaining districts, three of which are held by its allies and three by the opposition.

data.title: Asian Markets A Sea Of Red Amid Tech Sell-off
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - Asian stock markets are a sea of red on Friday, following the broadly negative cues on Wall Street overnight, dragged by markets in Taiwan, South Korea and Japan amid a sell-off in semiconductor and technology stocks on lingering concerns about where the AI trade goes from here. Commodity-related stocks also took a hit. Concerns of re-escalation in the Middle East also gripped the markets. Asian markets ended mostly lower on Thursday.

Traders are questioning whether heavy AI capital spending and debt will generate strong returns. Claude developer Anthropic's market debut on the NASDAQ also failed to lift broader AI sentiment.

US policymakers were concerned about the possible threat to the economy in the event of the current hyper-spending in building AI architectures by technology majors backfires and leads to massive job losses.

Increasing concerns of possible U.S. attacks on Iran renewed oil-linked inflation worries after the Iranian military continued to announce vessels hitting naval mines and catching fire while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Two super tankers that were carrying a total of more than 4 million barrels of crude oil caught fire.

Australian stock market is trading significantly lower on Friday, extending the losses in the previous six sessions, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 is falling to near the 8,600 level, with weakness across most sectors led by gold miners and technology stocks.

The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 Index is losing 138.70 points or 1.59 percent to 8,591.70, after hitting a low of 8,585.00 earlier. The broader All Ordinaries Index is down 138.40 points or 1.57 percent to 8,698.20. Australian stocks closed significantly lower on Thursday.

Among major miners, Mineral Resources is declining more than 2 percent and BHP Group is losing almost 2 percent, while Fortescue is gaining more than 2 percent and Rio Tinto is edging up 0.4 percent.

Oil stocks are mostly lower. Woodside Energy is slipping almost 1 percent, Origin Energy is edging down 0.3 percent, Santos is down more than 1 percent and Beach energy is losing more than 2 percent.

Among tech stocks, Afterpay and Square-owner Block and Xero are tumbling almost 7 percent each, while Zip is sliding almost 9 percent, Appen is declining more than 9 percent and WiseTech Global is slipping almost 6 percent.

Among the big four banks, Westpac is declining more than 2 percent, ANZ Banking is losing almost 2 percent, National Australia Bank is down more than 1 percent and Commonwealth Bank is slipping almost 1 percent.

Gold miners are weak. Evolution Mining is declining more than 4 percent, Northern Star Resources is losing almost 4 percent, Genesis Minerals is sliding almost 5 percent, Newmont is slipping almost 6 percent and Resolute Mining is down more than 2 percent.

In other news, shares in Monash IVF are plummeting more than 23 percent after it issued a full-year profit warning for fiscal 2027, projecting underlying net profit after tax to come in materially below fiscal 2026 and consensus estimates.

In the currency market, the Aussie dollar is trading at $0.665 on Friday.

The Japanese market is trading sharply lower on Friday, reversing the gains in the previous two sessions, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is tumbling 4.5 percent to below the 56,800 level, with weakness across most sectors led by index heavyweights and technology stocks.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 Index closed the morning session at 56,775.04, down 2,669.17 points or 4.49 percent, after hitting a low of 56,594.94 earlier. Japanese shares ended notably higher on Thursday.

Market heavyweight SoftBank Group is plunging almost 15 percent and Uniqlo operator Fast Retailing is edging down 0.5 percent. Among automakers, Toyota is edging down 0.2 percent and Honda is also edging down 0.4 percent.

In the tech space, Advantest is plunging almost 10 percent, Screen Holdings is sliding more than 8 percent and Tokyo Electron is tumbling more than 6 percent.

In the banking sector, Mizuho Financial, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial are all losing more than 2 percent each.

Among the major exporters, Mitsubishi Electric is losing almost 4 percent, Panasonic is tumbling more than 8 percent and Sony is edging down 0.1 percent, while Canon is edging up 0.2 percent.

Among other major losers, Ibiden and Mitsui Kinzoku are plummeting almost 13 percent each, while Furukawa Electric is plunging almost 12 percent. Kioxia Holdings and Fujikura are tumbling more than 11 percent each, while Kokusai Electric, Taiyo Yuden and Sumco are sliding almost 11 percent each. Resonac Holdings is slipping more than 10 percent, Sumitomo Metal Mining is falling more than 9 percent and Japan Tobacco is losing almost 9 percent.

Conversely, Tokio Marine is gaining almost 4 percent and MS&AD Insurance is adding almost 3 percent.

In economic news, overall consumer prices in Japan spiked 0.8 percent on month in October, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications said on Friday. That was well above forecasts for an increase of 0.3 percent following the flat reading in September. On a yearly basis, inflation was up 2.3 percent, above forecasts for 2.2 percent and up from 2.1 percent in the previous month.

Core CPI, which strips out the volatile costs of fresh food, was up 2.2 percent on year. That was shy of expectations for an increase of 2.3 percent and was up from 2.1 percent a month earlier.

In the currency market, the U.S. dollar is trading in the lower 159 yen-range on Friday.

Elsewhere in Asia, Taiwan and South Korea are plunging 6.2 and 4.6 percent, respectively. China, Singapore and Hong Kong are lower by between 1.7 and 2.0 percent each. New Zealand, Malaysia and Indonesia are down by between 0.5 to 0.9 percent each.

On Wall Street, stocks moved to the upside at the start of trading on Thursday but showed a substantial downturn over the course of the session. The major averages pulled back well off their early highs and firmly into negative territory.

The major averages all finished the day sharply lower. The Dow plummeted 1,101.11 points or 2.2 percent to 49.097.06, the Nasdaq plunged 550.69 points or 2.3 percent to 23,879.20 and the S&P 500 tumbled 147.80 points or 2 percent to 7,175.83.

The major European markets have all also moved to the downside on the day. While the German DAX Index slumped 1.1 percent, the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index slid by 0.9 percent and the French CAC 40 Index fell by 0.8 percent.

Crude oil prices edged higher on Thursday as fears of supply disruptions increased in the Strait of Hormuz. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery was up $0.17 or 0.20 percent at $83.43 per barrel.

data.title: Chicago soybeans set for weekly drop as dollar firms, wheat, corn decline
data.description:
Chicago soybeans declined for a fifth straight session on Friday and are set to book a weekly drop, weighed down by a stronger dollar that makes US soybeans less competitive.

Wheat futures declined, but are poised to log a second weekly gain, while corn fell on Friday and is likely to post a weekly loss.

The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was down 0.02% at $12.07-1/4 a bushel at 0332 GMT. The contract has lost 0.17% for the week.

The United States generated 758 million biodiesel blending credits (D4) in October, down from 792 million in September, while ethanol blending (D6) credits rose to 1.26 billion from 1.19 billion in September, according to Environmental Protection Agency data.

The US Department of Agriculture reported net export sales of US soybeans in the week ended November 12 at 1,501,000 metric tons for the current marketing year, within a range of trade expectations for 1 million to 2 million tons, and private sales of 200,844 metric tons of soybeans to Mexico for 2026/27 delivery.

Chicago wheat fell 0.42% at $5.92-1/2 a bushel and CBOT corn was down 0.28% at $ 4.51-1/4 a bushel

Argentina's 2026/27 wheat harvest is progressing with yields above expectations, the Buenos Aires grains exchange said, estimating the crop at 23.4 million tons, the country's second-highest production.

A group of South Korean flour mills has issued an international tender to purchase around 100,000 metric tons of milling wheat to be sourced from the United States only, while the Taiwan Flour Millers' Association has issued an international tender to purchase an estimated 89,000 metric tons of grade 1 milling wheat to be sourced from the United States, European traders said

Jordan's state grain buyer has issued an international tender to buy up to 120,000 metric tons of milling wheat which can be sourced from optional origins, European traders said on Thursday

Grain exports through Romania's Black Sea port of Constanta rose by double digits in the first 10 months of the year, the port authority said, helped by a good harvest, strong demand and Ukrainian exports passing through the port.

The International Grains Council has lowered its forecast for 2026/27 global corn production at 1.301 billion metric tons, down 6 million from last month's forecast, driven largely by downgrades for the US and Ukraine, and raised its 2026/27 world wheat crop outlook by 6 million tons to 826 million, reflecting upgrades in Argentina, Turkey, Egypt and Australia

Russia's annual capacity to ship grain from its ports on the Baltic Sea and in the Arctic has quadrupled since July following Ukrainian drone attacks in the Black Sea region, a senior executive at the country's railway monopoly said on Thursday.

data.title: Indonesia current account gap narrows significantly in Q3
data.description:
Indonesia's current account deficit narrowed significantly to 0.5% of gross domestic product in the third quarter, compared with a revised deficit of 3.4% of GDP in the previous three months, central bank data showed on Friday.

  • Its balance of payments recorded a surplus of $80 million in the third quarter, a swing from the $882 million deficit in the second quarter

  • The balance of payments surplus was mainly supported by a narrowing current account deficit amid a higher surplus in the non-oil and gas goods trade balance and a lower deficit in the oil and gas trade balance, the central bank added

  • The narrower current account deficit of $2 billion was driven by higher non-oil and gas exports amid rising prices of Indonesia's export commodities and lower energy imports

  • Indonesia's current account position is closely watched by investors and policymakers and often seen as an indicator of economic vulnerability, with the country exposed to capital outflows and weighing on the rupiah, which earlier this week hit another record low

  • Going forward, Bank Indonesia expects the balance of payments to remain favorable to support external resilience

  • It projects the current account deficit to remain low through improved exports and rising global commodity prices

data.title: India's Paytm takes 19.1% stake in Singapore's CardUp
data.description:
Indian fintech group One 97 Communications (BSE: 543396) , which operates Paytm, will invest up to INR2bn ($21.458mn) in subsidiaries of Singapore lender Funding Societies, beginning with a 19.1% stake in payments company CardUp, the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 19.

The board of Paytm Singapore, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary, approved the partnership with Funding Asia Group, which trades as Funding Societies, on the same day. The deal gives the Noida-based company a foothold in Singapore's digital payments market under its 'Partner Operated' model. Under this approach, Paytm supplies its acceptance platform and devices while a local partner runs sales, distribution and day-to-day merchant operations.

Paytm will earn licensing fees and a share of revenue while committing only limited capital, according to the filing. The first tranche of roughly INR1.62bn will buy the CardUp stake in cash in exchange for newly issued shares. The remaining INR380mn or so may go into another Funding Societies affiliate. The investments depend on confirmatory due diligence, corporate approvals and the signing of definitive documents, and the company expects to complete the acquisition by May 20, 2027.

Alongside the equity deal, Paytm will sign a business and technology agreement with CardUp to provide payments and lending technology in Singapore. The contract runs for an initial five years and can be renewed on terms both sides accept. Paytm will collect technology fees and a revenue share under the arrangement. Founded on October 5, 2015, CardUp operates in digital payments in Singapore. Its turnover reached INR2.99bn in calendar 2025, up from INR1.94bn in 2024 and INR1.04bn in 2023. According to the filing, neither CardUp nor Funding Societies is a related party of Paytm, which has no identified promoter.

Paytm also confirmed it had put a further INR5bn into its wholly owned unit Paytm Cloud Technologies, which then invested the same amount in Paytm Singapore. This followed an earlier disclosure dated October 26.

data.title: India opens firing ranges to Japanese missile drills after Tokyo 2+2 talks
data.description:
Japanese forces are to fire missiles on Indian ranges for the first time under a deal signed at the India-Japan 2+2 ministerial meeting in Tokyo on November 19, 2026.

India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh spent 90 minutes with Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, according to a statement by Japan's foreign ministry. A letter of intent signed alongside the talks opens Indian firing ranges to live-fire training by the Japan Self-Defense Forces, surface-to-ship missiles included, and the joint statement tells both defence bureaucracies to speed up the arrangements.

For New Delhi, the fourth round of these talks turned years of shared declarations into hardware and live rounds. India signs no mutual defence alliances, yet it now hosts Japanese fighter jets, trains with Japan's navy and is lining up its first purchase of Japanese naval technology. Each step answers the same two worries, a Chinese military budget several times its own, and an expanding Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy (PLA-N) footprint in the Indo-Pacific littoral region.

Kit, not communiques

The centrepiece is UNICORN, a Japanese shipborne integrated communications antenna. The two defence ministers called it the first defence equipment transfer project between their countries when they met in New Delhi in August. Tokyo now expects India's defence ministry to grant its Acceptance of Necessity, the formal opening step of an Indian procurement, by February 2027, under a 'Design with Japan, Make in India' label. India's Defence Research and Development Organisation and Japan's Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency are also to begin joint research on missiles and other advanced defence technology, the Indian defence ministry said after Singh's separate meeting with Koizumi, their third in 2026.

Japan Air Self-Defence Force fighters flew to India for the first time ever in 2026, they arrived on Indian shores to be a part of the Veer Guardian 26 exercise. In November 2026 the two navies also sailed together in Japan for the Malabar 2026 exercise, alongside their US and Australian counterparts, and in the bilateral JAIMEX26 drill. A maritime security memorandum signed in August commits Tokyo and New Delhi to work on mine countermeasures and to study designing and building warships together, a step beyond the agenda of the eighth defence policy dialogue in July.

The neighbour nobody named

China appears nowhere in the joint statement. The ministers nonetheless voiced 'grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions,' a charge Tokyo knows from experience. In late June Beijing put export curbs on 40 Japanese companies and research bodies. Both sides also restated their opposition to any attempt 'to unilaterally change the status quo', the standard formula for Chinese pressure at sea and on India's Himalayan frontier.

China spent $336bn on its armed forces in 2025, more than twice the combined $154bn of India and Japan, according to World Bank figures based on SIPRI data. Military spending across the Asia-Pacific rose by 8.1% last year, the fastest increase since 2009.

Military expenditure of China, India, Japan and Pakistan, 2015-2025, $bn at current prices. Source: World Bank, SIPRI via IntelliNews Lambda

India secured its usual line on Pakistan too. The ministers condemned 'cross-border terrorism' and named Lashkar-e-Tayyiba and Jaish-e-Mohammad, two Pakistan-based groups India blames for attacks in Kashmir, next to Al Qaeda and Islamic State.

Money behind the guns

Bilateral trade reached about $27.5bn in fiscal 2025-26, Japan is India's fifth-largest source of foreign direct investment, and Tokyo has pledged to invest JPY10 trillion ($62.5bn) in India over a decade. An economic security declaration adopted at the annual summit in July marks out semiconductors, critical minerals, clean energy and pharmaceuticals for joint projects, which New Delhi needs if it is to cut its reliance on Chinese supply chains.

India also brings a scale Japan no longer has. The IMF's October World Economic Outlook projects that India's economy will overtake Japan's in dollar terms in 2027, at $4.52 trillion against $4.47 trillion, and then keep pulling away.

Nominal GDP of India and Japan, 2018-2031, $ trillion; IMF projections from 2026. Source: IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2026 via IntelliNews Lambda

Insurance in the Quad

The Tokyo meeting came two days after Quad leaders met in Manila, and the ministers cast their bilateral work as a complement to the four-way grouping's agenda on maritime security, economic security, new technology and disaster relief. In April the Quad had looked dead in the water. Its revival gives the India-Japan pairing a wider frame, and the pairing gives the Quad a working core that does not depend on the mood in Washington.

Each side backed the other's claim to a permanent seat on a reformed UN Security Council, and their bids for non-permanent seats in 2028-29 and 2033-34. The two will mark 75 years of diplomatic relations in 2027, and the next 2+2 is due in India. For a New Delhi that refuses to join blocs, Japan has become the partner that brings technology, capital and the same worry about China without asking India to choose a camp.

data.title: Institutions pile back into US Bitcoin ETFs in Q3 after selling streak
data.description:
Institutional investment managers’ holdings of US Bitcoin exchange-traded funds climbed to a record high in the third quarter, as they reversed three straight quarters of net selling, according to regulatory filings.

The 13F filings, analyzed by Galaxy Research, show that the reporting companies added an equivalent of 49,229 Bitcoin (BTC) in the third quarter, outpacing the 47,054 Bitcoin they shed over the last three quarters combined. This lifted the reported total holdings to 356,491 BTC, the highest on record.

“The quarter’s accumulation was the work of a few dozen large institutions,” wrote Galaxy’s head of firmwide research Alex Thorn.

Quarterly 13F filings provide a point-in-time snapshot of US-listed securities held by reporting institutional investment managers. Thorn said half of the net addition of spot Bitcoin ETF shares came from advisors and wealth platforms.

Wells Fargo posted the largest increase, adding the equivalent of 14,636 Bitcoin, making it the largest institutional holder of spot Bitcoin ETPs. Other strong gainers included Brevan Howard, Bank of America, Millennium Management and Jane Street.

Largest holders of spot Bitcoin ETP positions in Q3. Source: Galaxy Research

“Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot Bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi previously told Cointelegraph, when the first batch of 13F filings had begun to come in.

The number of managers reporting a position in a spot Bitcoin ETF also rose for the first time in three quarters, increasing by 191 to 2,166.

This all came as Bitcoin gained about 43% in the third quarter, ending September at $83,621.

Meanwhile, Galaxy’s data shows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for the largest share of holdings reported by 13F filers, with the equivalent of 232,453 BTC held by the filers. This was followed by the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund.

Together, the two funds were responsible for 77% of all Bitcoin held by the reporting entities.

Bitcoin equivalent held by 13F filers. Source: Galaxy Research

US Bitcoin ETFs post two months of outflows

The record institutional holdings in Q3 contrast with more recent weakness in US spot Bitcoin ETFs, with net monthly outflows reaching $515 million in October and $2.9 billion of outflows month to date, according to TFTC’s Bitcoin ETF tracker.

Earlier in the month, Bitwise head of research André Dragosch told Cointelegraph he viewed the selling as “related to a short-term risk-off environment rather than a structural change in institutional sentiment.”

data.title: Rupee today: Indian currency opens at 93.20, gains over ₹1 this week against US dollar
data.description:
The rupee gained further on Friday, November 20, after the currency opened flat on Thursday. The market is pricing in Fed rate hikes, even as the US dollar strengthens.

The Indian currency opened at 93.20 per US dollar, marginally stronger than Thursday's (November 19) close of 93.29, marking a leap of 0.070 paise.

The Rupee has opened positive on three occasions, and flat yesterday. This week so far, the rupee has gained 1.04 paise.

WHERE IS THE RUPEE HEADED?

The influx of foreign capital into equity markets has also reduced pressure on the central bank to defend the rupee, enabling it to sharply scale back dollar sales after months of heavy intervention, a Reuters report said.

According to the same report, traders and analysts are monitoring for signs that exporters are converting more of their dollar earnings, alongside continued portfolio inflows, to assess how much further the rupee could strengthen.

So far, corporate activity appears mixed across lenders: some report increased exporter participation, while others continue to see elevated importer hedging and exporters largely staying on the sidelines.

DOLLAR's DAY

The US dollar was on track for a fourth consecutive weekly advance on Friday, November 20, as demand associated with Anthropic’s stock market debut strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve would continue raising interest rates.

MARKET MATTER

After two good sessions, the markets are now looking to maintain the momentum. However, GIFT Nifty so far has indicated a gap-down start to the day's proceedings, as Nifty aims for 25,500.

Asian markets have slumped steeply. Japan suffered the steepest declines, with the Nikkei 225 falling 4.54% and the broader Topix dropping 2.75%. South Korea’s Kospi slid 4.74%, while Hang Seng futures edged down 0.2%.

Anthropic shares started trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday in the largest public debut on record, then rose 17% on their first day.

Another key aspect that dictates the movement in the currency market: oil appears to be steadying above the $90 mark, trading around $93 per barrel.

data.description: The South Korean won and Taiwan dollar are expected to lead Asian currencies in 2027, supported by strong technology exports, ING says. data.title: Currency Check | Rupee opens higher at 93.20 per dollar; Asian peers trade mixed
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened higher on November 20, as a surge in foreign inflows into Indian assets offsets the traditional pressure that a deterioration in sentiment exerts on emerging-market currencies.

The rupee opened with a gain of 9 paise at 93.20 per dollar, compared with previous close of 93.29.

According to Finrex, rupee to open at 93.29 levels after FPI bought Rs. 7411 crores of shares yesterday, the dollar amount of which will be sold in the markets today. The IPO was not subscribed well so the flows may not be good enough. Precious metals all fell big time yesterday with Gold touching $ 3560 per ounce down by 1.80% and silver touching $ 41.75 per ounce down by 6% which is more than 14-month low amid FED rate hike certainty and an ongoing rout in the AI trade on Wall Street which weighed on the yellow metal.

Exporters if they get the upside beyond 93.50 should sell for their exports with premiums higher while importers may now wait to buy near to 93.00 levels. Nothing much was taken from the US-RussiaChina summit held yesterday, it added.

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar, with most regional currencies registering losses. The Philippine peso was the worst performer, declining 0.31%, followed by the Taiwan dollar, which fell 0.27%. The Chinese renminbi weakened 0.18%, while the South Korean won and Indonesian rupiah slipped 0.15% and 0.12%, respectively. The Malaysian ringgit edged down 0.03%.

On the positive side, the Japanese yen gained 0.19%, emerging as the best-performing currency in the region, while the Thai baht and Singapore dollar edged higher by 0.06% and 0.04%, respectively.

The dollar is headed for a fourth straight weekly gain as demand tied to the Anthropic PBC IPO further lifts the currency that has been supported by expectations of further Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes and elevated US

Treasury yields.

data.title: China's fuel oil exports for bunkering ease in October while imports rebound
data.description:
China's fuel oil exports, mainly for marine fuel bunkering, fell in October after a strong September, while fuel oil imports rebounded, customs data showed on Friday.

October export volumes totalled 1.62 million metric tons, or about 333,000 barrels a day, down 37% from September but up 32% from the same month a year ago, according to General Administration of Customs data.

Bunker export activity slowed in October with more vessels calling at regional Asian hub Singapore, which offered lower prices during most of October for the mainstay low-sulphur fuel grade than Zhoushan and Shanghai ports, market sources said.

Meanwhile, fuel oil imports into China, which typically head to refineries and the marine fuel blending pool, recovered to a seven-month high in October as feedstock demand improved.

Customs data showed imports totaled 1.95 million tons for October, up 72% from September and 4% higher than a year earlier.

data.title: Kuwait offers second gasoline cargo this month in FOB tender, document shows
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Kuwait Petroleum Corp has offered 34,000-35,000 metric tons of 93-octane non-oxygenated gasoline in a tender on a free-on-board (FOB) basis from its Mina Al-Ahmadi port, a document reviewed by Reuters showed on Friday.

The cargo is scheduled to load between December 9 and December 10, according to the tender, which closed on Wednesday.

The state-run refiner sold the same grade fuel for late-November loading at a premium of around $180 to $200 per ton to Middle East naphtha quotes, market participants said.

It was KPC's first gasoline offer via a tender after a gap of several months since the war in the Gulf broke out.

Oil companies typically do not comment on tenders.

data.title: CGI and Learning Links Foundation launch Centre of Excellence for AI & Innovation at MEI Polytechnic College
data.description:
Initiative to provide hands-on learning opportunities in AI and emerging technologies for more than 1,250 students

BENGALURU, India, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CGI (TSX: GIB.A) (), one of the largest independent IT and business consulting services firms in the world, has inaugurated the CGI Centre of Excellence for AI & Innovation at MEI Polytechnic College in Bengaluru, in collaboration with Learning Links Foundation (LLF). Designed, funded and strategically planned by CGI, the centre creates a dedicated space where students can learn, experiment, and develop practical solutions using emerging technologies.

The centre will provide hands-on learning opportunities to more than 1,250 students in artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, 3D design and printing, electronics and digital fabrication. Students will participate in project-based learning, technical challenges and innovation activities that help connect classroom concepts with practical applications. Equipped with development boards, sensors, embedded systems, robotic platforms, and comprehensive prototyping tools, the facility empowers students to build, test, and refine solutions to real-world problems.

"Access to technology can open new paths for students when it is paired with the opportunity to experiment, build and solve real problems," said Deepak Shenoy, Senior Vice-President and Business Unit Leader, Asia Pacific Global Delivery Center of Excellence, CGI. "Through this centre, we want students to engage with AI and emerging technologies in a practical and responsible way, and to build the confidence and skills to turn their ideas into solutions. This initiative reflects CGI's commitment to supporting the communities where we live and work by creating more equitable opportunities for the future."

"The CGI Centre of Excellence for AI & Innovation will give our students the opportunity to experience emerging technologies in a practical and engaging environment," said L. N. Reddy, Principal, MEI Polytechnic College. "It will complement their technical education by allowing them to experiment, build prototypes and develop solutions, while strengthening the confidence and problem-solving skills they will need in a rapidly changing technology landscape."

"The journey from classroom learning to real-world innovation begins with access to the right opportunities," said Sudha Priyadarshan, Senior Vice President, Learning Links Foundation. "Through this collaboration with CGI and MEI Polytechnic College, students will be able to explore AI, IoT, robotics and 3D printing through structured, hands-on learning. We look forward to supporting them as they develop future-ready skills and learn how to transform their ideas into working solutions."

About CGI

Founded in 1976, CGI is among the largest independent IT and business consulting services firms in the world. With 94,000 consultants and professionals across the globe, CGI delivers an end-to-end portfolio of capabilities, from strategic IT and business consulting to systems integration, managed IT and business process services and intellectual property solutions. CGI works with clients through a local relationship model complemented by a global delivery network that helps clients digitally transform their organizations and accelerate results. CGI Fiscal 2026 reported revenue is CA$16.57 billion and CGI shares are listed on the TSX (GIB.A) and the NYSE (GIB). Learn more at cgi.com.
